atoms.text: This setup allows the QueryForge SQL query engine to read raw web server logs from the bucket analytics-raw-logs-prod and write query results back to it. Add a statement to the bucket policy with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-raw-logs-prod/logs/*. In the same statement, grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-raw-logs-prod/query-results/*, so results are stored under a separate prefix from the input data. Set the Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/QueryForgeExecutionRole, which the QueryForge workgroup assumes when it runs a query. Add a second statement that grants s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN to the same role, with an s3:prefix condition limited to logs/ and query-results/. The role must also have an identity-based permissions policy that allows the same actions, because access within one account is evaluated from both sides. Confirm the role's trust policy lists the QueryForge execution environment as a trusted entity. After saving, run a test query against a sample table and check that a result file appears under query-results/ with the role listed as the uploader in the object's access log.

This setup allows the QueryForge SQL query engine to read raw web server logs from the bucket analytics-raw-logs-prod and write query results back to it. Add a statement to the bucket policy with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-raw-logs-prod/logs/*. In the same statement, grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-raw-logs-prod/query-results/*, so results are stored under a separate prefix from the input data. Set the Principal to the service principal queryforge.amazonaws.com, which is the identity the service uses when it accesses the bucket during a query. Add a second statement that grants s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN to the same service principal, with an s3:prefix condition limited to logs/ and query-results/. Add an aws:SourceAccount condition set to 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition matching arn:aws:queryforge:us-east-1:111122223333:workgroup/*, so only your workgroups can use the grant. No separate identity-based policy is required for the service principal. After saving, run a test query against a sample table and check that a result file appears under query-results/ with queryforge.amazonaws.com listed as the requester in the object's access log.

This policy lets the BatchLens distributed job runner read partitioned Parquet input files and write job output to the bucket batch-pipeline-data. Create a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::batch-pipeline-data/input/*. Add s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::batch-pipeline-data/output/*, because large output files are uploaded in multiple parts. Set the Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/BatchLensJobRole, which each job run assumes at startup. Add a Condition block with s3:x-amz-acl equal to bucket-owner-full-control for the PutObject action so the bucket owner keeps control of the output. Grant s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN to the same role, restricted by an s3:prefix condition to input/ and output/. The job role needs a matching identity-based policy, and its session duration must exceed the longest expected job runtime. Submit a small job against a test partition and confirm that output part files appear under output/ and that no objects are written outside that prefix.

Create a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::batch-pipeline-data/input/*. Add s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::batch-pipeline-data/output/*, because large output files are uploaded in multiple parts. Set the Principal to the service principal batchlens.amazonaws.com, which the service uses when it accesses the bucket for a job run. Add a Condition block with s3:x-amz-acl equal to bucket-owner-full-control for the PutObject action so the bucket owner keeps control of the output. Grant s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN to the same service principal, restricted by an s3:prefix condition to input/ and output/. Add aws:SourceAccount set to 222233334444 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:batchlens:us-west-2:222233334444:job/*, so requests from other accounts' jobs are denied. Submit a small job against a test partition and confirm that output part files appear under output/ and that no objects are written outside that prefix.

This scenario covers a data-owning account that stores source tables in the bucket shared-sales-datasets and lets the DataLens analytics service in another account query them. Add a statement to the bucket policy with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::shared-sales-datasets/tables/*. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::shared-sales-datasets/analysis-output/*, so the consuming team can store results next to the data it queries. Set the Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/DataLensAnalystRole, which belongs to the consuming account. Because the role is in a different account, the consuming account must also attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows the same actions on this bucket. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, with an s3:prefix condition limited to tables/ and analysis-output/. Avoid granting s3:DeleteObject, so output cannot be removed by the consuming role. Verify the setup by running a DataLens query from the consuming account and checking that the result object is written under analysis-output/.

This scenario covers a data-owning account that stores source tables in the bucket shared-sales-datasets and lets the DataLens analytics service query them on behalf of a consumer in another account. Add a statement to the bucket policy with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::shared-sales-datasets/tables/*. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::shared-sales-datasets/analysis-output/*, so the consuming team can store results next to the data it queries. Set the Principal to the service principal datalens.amazonaws.com. Because the bucket owner's account differs from the consumer's, restrict the grant with aws:SourceAccount set to 555566667777 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:datalens:eu-west-1:555566667777:project/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, with an s3:prefix condition limited to tables/ and analysis-output/. Avoid granting s3:DeleteObject, so output cannot be removed through the service. No identity-based policy is needed in the consuming account for this bucket access. Verify the setup by running a DataLens query from the consuming account and checking that the result object is written under analysis-output/.

This guide configures the bucket customer-events-encrypted so the PulseQuery engine can read event files and write aggregated results, with all objects encrypted using SSE-KMS. Add a bucket policy statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-events-encrypted/events/* to the principal. Add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-events-encrypted/aggregates/* in the same statement. Set the Principal to the IAM user arn:aws:iam::333344445555:user/pulsequery-batch-user, whose access keys are configured in the PulseQuery connection settings. Add a Condition with s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption equal to aws:kms, so any write that omits encryption is rejected. The user also needs kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on the key policy of the customer-managed key that protects the bucket. Grant s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition for events/ and aggregates/. Rotate the access keys on a fixed schedule and verify the setup by checking that a written aggregate reports aws:kms as its encryption type.

Add a bucket policy statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-events-encrypted/events/* to the principal. Add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-events-encrypted/aggregates/* in the same statement. Set the Principal to the service principal pulsequery.amazonaws.com, which the engine uses for requests it makes against the bucket. Add a Condition with s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption equal to aws:kms, so any write that omits encryption is rejected. The key policy of the customer-managed key that protects the bucket must also allow kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey for the same service principal. Grant s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition for events/ and aggregates/. Add aws:SourceAccount set to 333344445555 and verify the setup by checking that a written aggregate reports aws:kms as its encryption type.

This policy supports the ReportHarbor scheduled reporting service, which reads nightly warehouse exports and writes finished report files to the bucket finance-reporting-store. Create a statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-reporting-store/warehouse-export/*. Add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-reporting-store/reports/* so rendered CSV and PDF files are stored under a dedicated prefix. Set the Principal to the AWS account ID 666677778888 by using arn:aws:iam::666677778888:root, and delegate access to specific identities inside that account with IAM policies. The report scheduler runs under an IAM role in that account, and that role's policy must allow the same two actions. Grant s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition for warehouse-export/ and reports/. Do not grant access to other prefixes in the bucket, which hold unrelated finance records. After saving the policy, trigger a manual report run and confirm that the output file appears under reports/ with the expected date in its key.

This policy supports the ReportHarbor scheduled reporting service, which reads nightly warehouse exports and writes finished report files to the bucket finance-reporting-store. Create a statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-reporting-store/warehouse-export/*. Add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-reporting-store/reports/* so rendered CSV and PDF files are stored under a dedicated prefix. Set the Principal to the service principal reportharbor.amazonaws.com, so access is granted to the service itself and not to a whole account. Add aws:SourceAccount set to 666677778888 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:reportharbor:us-east-2:666677778888:schedule/*, which limits the grant to schedules you own. Grant s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition for warehouse-export/ and reports/. Do not grant access to other prefixes in the bucket, which hold unrelated finance records. After saving the policy, trigger a manual report run and confirm that the output file appears under reports/ with the expected date in its key.

This guide covers a TransformGrid ETL pipeline that reads raw CSV files from a landing area and writes cleaned Parquet files to the bucket ingest-lakehouse. Add a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::ingest-lakehouse/landing/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::ingest-lakehouse/curated/*. Set the Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/TransformGridEtlRole, which the pipeline assumes for each scheduled run. Add a separate Deny statement for all principals when aws:SecureTransport is false, so every request must use TLS. Grant s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN to the role, restricted to the landing/ and curated/ prefixes. The role's identity-based policy should mirror these permissions and should not include s3:DeleteObject, which preserves the original landing files. Use a lifecycle rule on landing/ to expire processed files after 30 days instead. Run the pipeline on a test file and check that the Parquet output appears under curated/ and that the input is unchanged.

This setup gives interactive notebook sessions in the NoteSpan analytics workspace access to reference datasets and a place to write intermediate results in the bucket research-notebooks-data. Add a policy statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::research-notebooks-data/reference/*. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::research-notebooks-data/scratch/* for session output. Set the Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/NoteSpanSessionRole, which every notebook session assumes. Because this role is shared, include an s3:ListBucket statement on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition limited to reference/ and scratch/. The identity-based policy attached to the role must allow the same actions, and the role's session name should include the user identifier for audit purposes. Add a lifecycle rule that expires objects under scratch/ after 7 days to limit storage growth. Start a notebook session, read a reference file, write a result to scratch/, and verify the object's requester in the access logs.

Add a policy statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::research-notebooks-data/reference/*. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::research-notebooks-data/scratch/* for session output. Set the Principal to the service principal notespan.amazonaws.com, which the workspace uses when sessions access the bucket. Include an s3:ListBucket statement on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition limited to reference/ and scratch/. Add aws:SourceAccount set to 888899990000 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:notespan:us-east-1:888899990000:workspace/*, so only your workspaces are covered. Add a lifecycle rule that expires objects under scratch/ after 7 days to limit storage growth. Start a notebook session, read a reference file, write a result to scratch/, and verify in the access logs that the requester is notespan.amazonaws.com.

This guide allows the LogPrism log analytics service to read storage access logs and write hourly summary files to the bucket ops-access-logs. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::ops-access-logs/raw/*. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::ops-access-logs/hourly-summaries/* in the same statement. Set the Principal to the IAM user arn:aws:iam::999900001111:user/logprism-service-user, which LogPrism uses through stored credentials in its data source configuration. Grant s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition for raw/ and hourly-summaries/. Raw logs are organized by date, so list requests should use the prefix raw/YYYY/MM/DD/ to limit scan time. The user's identity-based policy must permit the same actions, and the credentials should be rotated at least every 90 days. Run the first summary job for one hour of data and confirm a summary file is written under hourly-summaries/ with a matching timestamp in its key.

Set the Principal to the service principal logprism.amazonaws.com, which LogPrism uses when it reads and writes objects for a data source. Grant s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition for raw/ and hourly-summaries/. Raw logs are organized by date, so list requests should use the prefix raw/YYYY/MM/DD/ to limit scan time. Run the first summary job for one hour of data and confirm a summary file is written under hourly-summaries/ with a matching timestamp in its key.
